3.1 Rule. A patient who does not attend two consecutive booked appointments without notice is discharged to the referrer. The clinic writes to the patient and the referrer within five working days of the second non-attendance.
3.2 Exception. Clause 3.1 does not apply to a patient who is under 18 years of age at the date of the second non-attendance, or who has an active safeguarding alert; such cases are referred to the clinical lead for review instead of discharge.
3.3 Appointments cancelled by the hospital, and appointments rescheduled at the hospital's request, are disregarded when counting consecutive appointments; they neither count as non-attendance nor break the sequence.
3.4 Inpatient ward attendances and telephone follow-ups are out of scope of this policy and are handled under OP-09.
4. Definitions. "Consecutive" refers to the patient's booked appointments in the clinic in date order after disregarding those in clause 3.3. "Referrer" is the practice named on the original referral. Where the clinic letter and the electronic appointment record show different appointment times, the electronic appointment record governs.
6. Amendment history. Issue 6, effective 1 February 2026: in clause 3.1 the words "without notice" mean without notice received by the clinic at least 24 hours before the appointment time. Under issue 5 any notice before the appointment time, however short, prevented an occasion from counting as non-attendance.

question.instructions: Under OP-07, should the clinic now discharge this patient to the referrer? Answer yes or no.

criteria.true: OP-07 requires discharge to the referrer on these facts.
criteria.false: OP-07 does not require discharge; the case falls outside clause 3.1 or within an exception.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: Under issue 6, notice less than 24 hours before the appointment does not prevent an occasion counting as non-attendance, so the 14 April call at 08:10 for a 09:30 appointment (electronic record governs over the letter's 11:00) is a non-attendance. provenance.why_hard: Three separate facts each look like they rescue the patient (same-day notice, a hospital cancellation in between, a date of birth close to the age threshold), and each fails only when read against a different clause.

POLICY EXTRACT — Halcyon Air Denied Boarding Compensation Policy, version 2026.1
2.1 Rule. A passenger holding a confirmed reservation who is denied boarding against their will because the flight is oversold receives compensation at the full amount set out in the compensation table for the route distance band.
2.2 Reduced compensation. Where the passenger is re-routed and the scheduled arrival of the alternative flight is within two hours of the original scheduled arrival, compensation is half the full amount.
2.3 Exception. No compensation is due to a passenger who is denied boarding because they did not complete check-in by the check-in deadline, did not present at the boarding gate by the gate closure time, or lacked valid travel documents.
2.4 Passengers who voluntarily surrender their seat in exchange for benefits offered by Halcyon Air are not entitled to compensation under this policy.
2.5 Disruption caused by weather or air traffic control restrictions is handled under the Delay and Cancellation Policy, which provides rebooking and care but no compensation.
3. Definitions. "Check-in deadline" means the time by which check-in must be completed. "Completed check-in" means the time a boarding pass is issued to the passenger, whether at a desk, kiosk or through the mobile application. Bag drop is not check-in. "Gate closure time" is 20 minutes before scheduled departure.
4. Amendment 2026.1, effective 1 May 2026. The check-in deadline for international flights in clause 2.3 is changed from 45 minutes to 60 minutes before scheduled departure. Domestic flights remain at 45 minutes.
